"""Print the front-matter keys of every kernel skill and its copies as w2/integrate has them (keys only)."""
import subprocess
import yaml

names = ["adopt", "audit", "change", "checkpoint", "discovery", "orchestration", "planning", "retrieval",
         "test-design", "qa-review"]
roots = ["template/governance/kernel/skills", ".claude/skills", ".rulesync/skills", "template/.rulesync/skills"]
for n in names:
    for r in roots:
        rel = f"{r}/{n}/SKILL.md"
        p = subprocess.run(["git", "show", f"w2/integrate:{rel}"], capture_output=True, text=True)
        if p.returncode:
            print(rel, "ABSENT")
            continue
        t = p.stdout
        end = t.find("\n---", 3)
        front = yaml.safe_load(t[3:end]) if t.startswith("---") else None
        keys = sorted(front) if isinstance(front, dict) else front
        meta = front.get("metadata") if isinstance(front, dict) else None
        print(rel, keys, "metadata:", sorted(meta) if isinstance(meta, dict) else meta)

discoveries: (1) No kernel skill on integrate or on the base declares `output`. On integrate no kernel skill or copy has a permission field; only the six openspec `.claude` copies carry `allowed-tools`. (2) Conflict for later tickets: rulesync carries only `metadata` into the `.claude` copy, and the closed set allows only `metadata.version`. So a generated copy cannot carry `output`, yet W2-120's line refuses a skill without an output class and reads every generated copy. Either `metadata.output` is allowed in copies, or W2-120 reads output from the kernel source only. (3) The test-design folder on the base already cites DEC-979, and the orchestration folder already cites DEC-953; those cases fail on the missing statement instead.

It cannot see a write named without a code span. (2) The failure-1 permission-field case and the three planted cases pass on the base by design: the first guards the new text, the others test the check, as failure-2's do. (3) The brief's TMPDIR, /tmp/gov-os-lead-W2-11, is not writable from my sandbox, so pytest quietly used the worktree root (`pytest-of-usain/`). Only an untracked folder appeared; I removed it and committed nothing from it.
lessons: The worker sandbox cannot write the lead's TMPDIR. Check `git status` after each run, or give workers a TMPDIR inside the sandbox. Pytest's assertion introspection can print a file's text into the log. My checks now assert on precomputed booleans so failures show only my message; the next designer should do the same so implementation text never reaches the log.

Recommendation: allow `metadata.output` in generated copies only, with the template's closed set unchanged. Confidence medium-low; it is W2-120's and G13's question.
